Nrp1 deletion in GnRH neurons enhances GnRH neuron survival and migration, which leads to early prepubertial weight gain, premature sexual attraction, and precocious sexual maturation.
neuropilin‐1 expression is required for normal migration of GnRH neurons, which results in a normal pattern of sexual attraction and puberty.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

neuropilin‐1 signaling in GnRH neurons controls the timing of puberty, by regulating the number and migration of GnRH neurons, and their integration into the hypothalamic circuit, which results in early prepuberty weight gain, and premature attraction to male odor and precocious puberty.

the timing of puberty can be regulated by the central nervous system itself through the regulation of GnRH neuron migration and function, and that this regulation might be mediated by semaphorin–neuropilin signaling.
GnRH neurons, through neuropilin‐semaphorin signalling, regulate the timing of puberty, and thus, act as a bridge between reproductive and metabolic axes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

GnRH neurons, which are not known to be influenced by peripheral signals, might actually regulate peripheral adiposity and behavior, and that the timing of puberty might be controlled by GnRH neuron‐mediated changes in adiposity and attraction to males.
the timing of puberty is not only determined by the peripheral state but also by intrinsic factors within the brain, which can influence peripheral metabolism and behavior.
